paper_metadata.title: Influence of Mo and B additions in intermetallic near-Fe3Al alloys on microstructure and mechanical properties

evidence.quote: A potential candidate is the quinary Fe – Al – Mo – Ti – B system which is strengthened by solid solution and eutectic borides.

parameters.cooling_method: preheated furnace cooling to room temperature

evidence.quote: Alloys were produced by centrifugal investment casting (IC) into insulated ceramic molds made from Al2O3. The melts were homogenized for 2 min under vacuum and the molds were preheated to a minimum of 1000 ◦C before casting. After centrifugal casting, the hot molds were cooled in a preheated furnace to room temperature to minimize cracking.
The diffraction pattern of the Fe3Al matrix was indexed using the ordered cubic D03 structure (Fm-3m, space group 225).
The secondary phase is a complex boride which was assigned to the Mo2FeB2 structure according to Li et al. [20].

attributes.location: outer casting walls growing towards center

evidence.quote: Columnar-like grains can be recognized growing from the outer casting walls towards the center, where grains possess a mostly non-equiaxed and irregular morphology typical for cast structures.
WDS measurements indicated particles with TiB2 composition with additions of Mo.
A potential candidate is the quinary Fe – Al – Mo – Ti – B system which is strengthened by solid solution and eutectic borides.
